headline: SITCON rises to 2: patched Zyxel GS1900 switches still exploitable; OpenSSH emergency fix on Alpine; WordPress KEV due today

bullets.text: Changed: SITCON rose from 3 to 2 (SEVERE). One KEV addition in 72 hours and 4 critical reports in 48 hours; Zyxel GS1900 is the top story (4 outlets). The last 7 days still scored 0.62x the 90-day average.
New, OpenSSH, 3 outlets: OpenSSH issued an emergency fix for a flaw that lets long passwords bypass SSH authentication on Alpine Linux.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Zyxel's fix for a zero-day used to hack nearly 1,000 switches did not block the in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441); SecurityWeek reports the hacks blamed on a patched flaw were a zero-day. Root command execution is possible.
Due today, WordPress Core: CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a TOCTOU race condition exploited for RCE, added 2026-11-03 with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.

Still active: cPGuard autoupdate hijacked in the OpsShield supply-chain attack to deploy a backdoor (4 outlets); a patched Apple flaw, CVE-2024-27834, is exploited to deliver info-stealers (KEV due 2026-11-18).

New breaches: ransomware disrupted Wi-Fi and on-site computers at Queens Public Library; DigiCert disclosed a breach exposing customer information and identity documents; DreamHost confirmed exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions.

actions: Apply the OpenSSH emergency fix on Alpine Linux hosts now and restrict SSH password auth until patched.
Treat Zyxel GS1900 switches as exposed even after patching: restrict management access, check for compromise, watch for a new fix.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 today (KEV due 2026-11-06).
cPGuard users: hunt for the backdoor delivered via autoupdate and rotate credentials on affected servers.
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18) and Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935 (KEV due 2026-11-13).
DreamHost customers: rotate FTP and webmail credentials and end active sessions.
